cases.rationale: Clean unreacted-precursor regression control at the low-temperature end: equimolar ZnO and WO3 with full references, high counts, known zero and specimen effects disabled. It separates basic phase retrieval and mass quantitation from nuisance-profile failures.

Moderate full-reference partial CaCO3 reaction: major scheelite CaWO4 with weak residual calcite and WO3. The equimolar Ca:W balance is preserved, while the approximately 6 wt% carbonate tests minor-phase persistence under ordinary displacement, profile, texture and reference mismatch effects.

Hard full-reference four-phase CuO reaction with major triclinic CuWO4, cation-rich Cu3WO6 intermediate, residual WO3 and approximately 2.4 wt% CuO. Molar coefficients preserve global Cu:W = 1:1; the case targets overlap, low-abundance detection and persistence through a complex refinement without making reference adaptation the bottleneck.

Easier missing-reference adaptation case: major scheelite SrWO4 with residual SrCO3 and WO3 in a balanced partial reaction. All SrWO4 entries are withheld; the nearest surviving framework is tier 1 CaWO4 (COD 7219229, Ca->Sr, framework RMS 0.0226, 4.3% cell mismatch), so chemical substitution and lattice refinement should suffice.

Harder missing-reference adaptation paired with c04: major wolframite ZnWO4 plus residual ZnO and WO3, globally Zn:W balanced. Same-composition records and every one-substitution framework match are withheld. The nearest survivor is tier 2 NbInO4 (COD 1524100, In->Zn and Nb->W, framework RMS 0.0106, 4.2% cell mismatch), requiring a two-site chemical adaptation rather than direct retrieval.

Missing secondary-intermediate case for a mixed-valence manganese-oxide precursor: major wolframite MnWO4, approximately 15.5 wt% cation-rich Mn3WO6 and compensating WO3 preserve global Mn:W = 1:1. Only the Mn3WO6 record is withheld; tier 1 Mn3TeO6 (COD 2211528, Te->W, framework RMS 0.0183, 1.86% cell mismatch) survives. This tests whether adaptation is attempted for a secondary phase after the main phases already fit much of the pattern.
